title: Binary Length with a Space Bound
statement: There exist a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, on every Boolean word $x$, $M$ halts within $c(|x|+1)$ steps and outputs the little-endian binary representation of $|x|$. For every such $x$ and every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, its computation through step $t$ uses at most $c\bigl(\operatorname{size}(|x|)+1\bigr)$ work-tape cells, where $\operatorname{size}$ is the natural-number size function.
hypotheses_covered: Existence of a finite Turing machine over Booleans
Existence of a natural-number constant c
Computes the binary representation of |x| within c(|x|+1) steps on every input
For every input and every t, space through step t is at most c(size(|x|)+1)
